To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cavity photon contribution to the effective electron-electronic interaction can be understood in term of the cavity photons modifying the polarization of the charge distribution in the double quantum dot potential.

the presence of a single cavity photon field in a double quantum dot system leads to a more repulsive effective electron-electron Coulomb interaction and that this can be reduced by exciting quadrupolar collective modes.
the effective interaction of parallel quantum dots is enhanced by a cavity photon field, and that the effective repulsive interaction can be reduced by collective excitations of the system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of electrons in a double quantum dot system in a cavity.
cavity quantum electrodynamics (cavity QED) of electrons.
the effective electron interaction in the presence of cavity photon modes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cavity photon field can be used to control the effective interaction of an electron pair in a double parallel dot system.
the cavity photon field can modify the effective electron-electronic interaction in the parallel quantum dot system.
the effective electron–electron interaction is more repulsive in presence of a cavity mode, and can be reduced by classical external electric field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cavity photon field can be utilized to tune and manipulate the effective Coulomb repulsion of electrons in parallel dots, which is a key parameter for the design of quantum information systems.
the cavity photons modify the effective interaction between the two electrons in a parallel double dot system.
the cavity photons can be used for controlling the electron-electron interaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the cavity photon field is expected to play an important role in the effective interaction between electrons confined in a quantum dot system, and can be controlled through classical electric field excitation.
cavity photons can lead to a modification of the Coulomb interaction between electrons in parallel quantum dot systems.
the effective Coulomb interaction between electrons in parallel double quantum dots is modified by a single cavity photon mode.
